outcomeNote: Citation of a baraita elaborating the mishna.

segments.he: וּמְבָרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ שְׁמוֹנֶה בְּרָכוֹת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל הַתּוֹרָה — כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁמְּבָרְכִים בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, עַל הָעֲבוֹדָה, וְעַל הַהוֹדָאָה, וְעַל מְחִילַת הֶעָוֹן כְּתִיקְנָהּ. וְעַל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְעַל הַכֹּהֲנִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, וְעַל שְׁאָר תְּפִלָּה.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna: «And» the High Priest «recites eight blessings» after the reading. «The Sages taught» in a baraita that these are the eight blessings: The blessing «concerning the Torah» is recited «in the» usual «way one recites a blessing in the synagogue:» Who gives the Torah; The three blessings: «concerning the» Temple «service, concerning thanksgiving, and concerning pardon of iniquity,» are all recited «according to their established forms» in the prayers; The blessing «concerning the Temple in and of itself;» The blessing «concerning the priests in and of themselves;» The blessing «concerning the Jewish people in and of itself;» The blessing «concerning the rest of the prayer.»

moves.about: mishna lemma: the High Priest recites eight blessings

positions.claim: the eight blessings are Torah, service, thanksgiving, pardon, Temple, priests, Israel, rest of prayer
